children: Australia's Unemployment Rate Climbed in August
SYDNEY--Australia's unemployment rate rose unexpectedly in August, despite a sharp increase in employment over the month.
The jobless rate climbed to 4.6% in August from 4.5% in July, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Thursday. Financial markets had expected no change in the unemployment rate.
Employment jumped by 39,500 over the month, with the discrepancy in the data stemming from a rise in the number of people looking for work, the ABS said.
The workforce participation rate, which counts the number of people employed or looking for work, rose to 67.1% in August from 66.9% in July, the data showed.
Australia's economy has been battling higher fuel costs, rising interest rates, and slumping confidence for much of the year, causing the job market to slow in recent months.
Still, the higher jobless rate likely won't prevent the Reserve Bank of Australia from raising interest rates further at its policy meeting next week.
Over the last month, the RBA has highlighted that inflation remains too high, while warning it could climb further due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and strong demand in the tech sector.
Part-time employment rose by 45,800 people in August, while full-time employment fell by 6,300 people, the ABS said.
